title: Is Claude and Chat GPT really that much better for making games compared to Gemini?
author: SnooPeanuts9744
selftext:
Lately, I've been working on a 3D Roguelike Unity game using Gemini. It’s been pretty neat and practically free because I managed to get a ton of Pro subscription months through student verification. Because of that, paying $20/month for another service feels like a waste, especially living in a developing country where $20 hits a bit harder. But since I see almost nobody on this sub using Gemini, I wanted to share my workflow and ask: **Is the grass actually greener on the Claude/GPT side?**

\- **Coding**: I use Gemini Flash (High) / 3.7 and 3.8. It works pretty well if you break everything down into small tasks and separate modules. Yes, it makes mistakes, but it's usually capable of fixing itself. However, I’ve reached the point where I have to glue all those modules together, and that's the main reason I'm thinking about switching. Also, Flash can get pretty slow, taking around 15–25 minutes to complete a  prompt involving many files, even longer if it's a stubborn bug neither of us can figure out. On the upside, I never run out of weekly tokens/usage.

\- **UI & Icons**: Most of the UI is fully procedural. The icons were made with Nano; they are relatively simple (like website SVG icons), so providing an example helps ensure consistency. The only headache is the borders, it never respects the border layout in 1:1 images, no matter how explicitly I tell it to.

\- **Models**: Nano Banana + Tripo, mostly used for small props, clothes, hair, and character accessories.

\- **Animation**: I started out modifying free, cheap, or on-sale animations (from Mixamo, Itch, Unity Asset Store, or asset packs on Humble Bundle / Fanatical). Recently, I've been giving Argon a try. While it's not perfect, the artifacts are usually minimal and pretty easy to touch up manually. The main downside is that it burns through the 5-hour limit in just 3–5 prompts.

Has anyone here made the switch from Gemini to Claude/GPT for game dev? Is the coding quality and integration really worth the extra cost, or am I just hitting architectural bottlenecks inherent to large scripts?

*And if you're asking why I didn't include any screenshots/images, it's because I can't, it's an NSFW game. Plus, I want to keep the fact that I use AI under wraps, at least for the assets. People still demonize AI way too much, even when the vast majority of the work is human-made and the AI-generated content is minimal.*

comments.author: space64-llc
comments.body:
I wouldn’t spend the $20 just because Gemini gets mentioned less here. If it’s working for you, that matters more than which tool everyone else is posting about.

The “now glue all these modules together” stage is worth looking at first. Individually reasonable scripts can make different assumptions about who owns state, how events work, or when things get initialised. Before asking for another fix, have it trace one complete flow—spawning an enemy, damaging it, killing it and awarding loot—and identify where the scripts disagree. Then fix one connection at a time.

We’ve used ChatGPT to help develop Chess Folk, if you want an example of a released game built with that assistance. I’m one of the developers, though, and that isn’t a comparison against Gemini on your project.

If you do try another service, give it one integration bug you already understand and compare the result. Did it find the cause, keep the changes focused and explain how to verify the fix? That’s a more useful test than whether it produces an impressive amount of code.
